correctness.rationale: For an ordinary identifying code of size k in a cubic 24-vertex graph, all 24 nonempty closed-neighborhood signatures are distinct; at most k are singletons and the sum of their sizes is \(4k\), hence \(5k\ge48\) and \(k\ge10\). Standalone exact C++ exhaustive enumeration covers all 1,961,256 size-ten and 2,496,144 size-eleven subsets, checking both signatures and intersection with the 300 closed-neighborhood/symmetric-difference tests for every candidate. These two checks agree globally: zero size-ten and 384 size-eleven codes. A separately constructed LCF graph and exact enumeration of all 32 automorphisms partitions the 384 into 13 stated orbits. The actual bundled verifier was executed with all assertions passing. Neither finite samples nor log output alone substitute for the complete bounded enumeration implemented and reviewed.

value.rationale: The McGee graph is a uniquely extremal natural cubic \((3,7)\)-cage, with exceptional failure of vertex-transitivity. Determining the exact minimum number of sensors needed to distinguish every vertex and enumerating all 13 geometric symmetry classes is mathematically meaningful: the class multiplicities and intersections with its 8+16 intrinsic vertex partition are not supplied by girth, regularity or graph automorphism order. This is a complete finite classification with explicit reusable certificates; no generalized infinite theorem is claimed or required.
